## Summary

The audit runner (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) crashes with an unhandled `TypeError` in `_map_gaps_to_children` (line ~2930) when a Phase 2 deep-analysis AC result carries `evidence` as a `dict` instead of a string:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "audit_runner.py", line 5343, in <module>
    raise SystemExit(main())
  ...
  File "audit_runner.py", line 2930, in _map_gaps_to_children
    for m in re.finditer(r"([\w./-]+\.\w+)(?::\d+)?", evidence):
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'dict'
```

`_map_gaps_to_children` does `evidence = r.get("evidence", "") or ""` — a truthy dict passes through unvalidated into `re.finditer`, which requires str/bytes. The runner dies mid-run: no report is persisted, no verdict emitted, and the run is wasted (Phase 1 + Phase 2 deep analysis already consumed ~11 minutes).

discovered-from:LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
python3 /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog
```

The Phase 2 model returned an AC verdict whose `evidence` field is a JSON object (e.g. structured `{file, line, note}`) rather than the expected `path/file:line` string.

## Suggested fix

- Normalize evidence defensively in `_map_gaps_to_children`: `evidence = r.get("evidence", "")`; `if not isinstance(evidence, str): evidence = str(evidence) or ""` (or json-dumps dicts to salvage file refs).
- Consider the same guard anywhere else evidence is consumed with regex (audit report assembly, gap mapping, child reuse parsing).
- Optionally: strengthen the Phase 2 prompt to require `evidence` be a string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_map_gaps_to_children` (and any sibling evidence consumers) tolerate non-string evidence without crashing.
- [ ] A unit test feeds an AC result with dict evidence and asserts no exception and a sensible (conservative) mapping.
- [ ] Re-running the audit of LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP (or any item whose Phase 2 returns dict evidence) completes and persists.

## Resolution (2026-09-20)

**Status: closed as fixed, per producer decision.**

The bug described in this item was already fixed on `dev` in commit
`1a6539a8` — *"SA-0MSKM2LSP006L0K8: Implementation complete"* (2026-08-15) —
before this intake was run. The commit added the defensive `_evidence_text()`
helper and applied it at `_map_gaps_to_children()` and every other
regex/substring evidence consumer in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
together with six regression tests (dict-evidence gap mapping,
sibling-consumer tolerance, Phase 2 normalisation, end-to-end persist).

**Acceptance criteria status**

- [x] `_map_gaps_to_children` (and sibling evidence consumers) tolerate
  non-string evidence without crashing — done via `_evidence_text()`.
- [x] Unit test feeds an AC result with dict evidence and asserts no exception
  and a sensible (conservative) mapping — done.
- [x] Re-running an audit whose Phase 2 returns dict evidence completes and
  persists — covered by `test_dict_evidence_completes_and_persists`, which
  passes on `dev`.

**Verification:** the six regression tests from commit `1a6539a8` pass on
`dev`; `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlinks to `skill/`, so the installed runner is
identical to the repo copy.

**Producer decision (2026-09-20):** item closed as already-fixed; the
residual debug-log hardening question was answered N/A (out of scope).

# Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: phases `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` and `_phase_fetch_and_cq` fail to use commit references stored only in comments, and treat arbitrary hex found in prose as cherry-pick candidates, producing a spurious merge-gate blocker and a false-negative audit.

Discovered during audit of OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm, `--force` run, work already present in `origin/dev`).

## Symptom

- Work item has no feature branch and no commit in its description; its real implementation commit is referenced only in a comment (e.g. `235ef18` for OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S).
- Merge gate logs `integrating (branch=none, commits=[9b0f...])` then fails: `git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object` and blocks the audit.
- `9b0f500f...` is a *foreign* autiobook reference pinned in the description (reference, not a commit in the owning repo). `235ef18` (the real commit) is never discovered.

## Root cause

1. **Comments not fetched early for merge gate.** `_phase_fetch_and_cq` loads the top-level `comments` from `wl show` into a separate binding, but `ctx.work_item.get("comments", [])` (or the equivalent) is still the default empty list when the merge gate resolves evidence, so commit shas referenced only in comments are never seen. Reproduction: `wl show OSL-... --children --json` has `workItem.comments` absent while top-level `comments` holds the Map commit.

2. **Over-broad hex extraction.** `re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE)` picks up arbitrary hex strings (foreign repo refs, docs examples) and enqueues them as cherry-pick targets. The failing run treated `9b0f500f...` (from `9b0f500f11f...`, an autiobook pin) as a required candidate and failed closed when that object was absent.

3. **Interaction.** Because (1) left `commits=[foreign_hex]`, (2) caused the integration failure path; the item *was* already on `origin/dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`) but was rejected.

## Proposed fix

- Fetch and bind `comments` on `ctx` before `_phase_merge_gate` (or pass `comments` into `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`).
- Filter integration candidates to objects that actually exist or are already ancestors of `origin/dev` (e.g. `git cat-file -e <sha>` / `rev-parse --verify` check, or skip foreign shas that are not ancestors and not branch tips), so that documentation hex cited as reference does not force cherry-pick.
- Optionally, scope hex extraction to producer-attributed commit citations (e.g. `see commit <hex>`) rather than every hex token in prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A work item whose only commit citation is in a top-level comment (no branch, no 7+ hex in description) is correctly merged-gated: evidence resolves the commented commit and `containment` verifies it against `origin/dev`.
2. Hex tokens that are not objects in the owning repo (or are cited only as foreign-repo pinned references, not deliverable commits) do not cause `fatal: bad object` or a spurious merge-gate block.
3. Existing behaviour for feature-branch and description-referenced commits is preserved (regression tests).
4. No new behaviour breaks `wl show` clients: comment binding is done in the audit runner only.

## Evidence

- Failing run (`open_source_llm`, `235ef18` already in `origin/dev`):
  ```
  Merge gate: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S work NOT present in origin/dev — integrating (branch=none, commits=["9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b"])
  git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object
  ```
- Manual verification: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`.
- Stored blocker audit: `wl audit-show OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S --json` (open_source_llm).

## Related

- Proposer work item: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm). See its audit trail and producer-review comment id OSL-C0MTQA3R4E0084LBY.
- Worktree remains at `open_source_llm/.worklog/worktrees/audit-merge-OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S` (remove manually once triaged).
data.title: Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

# Raise full-suite per-command timeout so audit auto-execute can complete

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem Statement

During the automated audit of SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0, the audit runner's automatic
full-suite verification invoked the test skill (`run_tests.py`) to execute the
full suite at HEAD. The pytest command hit the default per-command timeout of
600s and was killed, preventing a green full-suite cache entry from being
produced. This meant audit-dependent ACs could only be marked `partial`.

## Current State

- **`.pi/test-config.json`** already exists with `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}`,
  added under **SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV** (commit 715806bb). The measured full
  suite wall-clock is **~412s**, well within the 1500s timeout.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the `.pi/test-config.json`
  mechanism generically (the `timeoutPerCommand` field, its interaction with
  `suiteCommands`, and how the audit runner honours it).
- A **pre-existing test failure** (`test_plan_helpers.py` — Medium risk no
  longer triggers approval per commit a9d8b8b9, but the test still parametrised
  "Medium") blocks AC6. This is a separate issue.

## Users

1. **Automated agents** (audit skill, test skill) — need the full suite to run
   to completion so audit auto-execute can verify ACs.
2. **Developers** running `/skill:test` — need the timeout to reflect real
   full-suite wall-clock time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`.pi/test-config.json`** exists with `timeoutPerCommand` set to a value
   sufficient for the full suite to finish (current value: 1500s; measured
   wall-clock: ~412s, providing ~3.6x safety margin). No `suiteCommands`
   override — command detection uses existing conventions.
2. `run_tests.py --type full --force` completes within the new timeout at HEAD.
3. The audit runner's auto-execute path honours the override (no 600s kill).
4. The change is project-local: no other repository's timeout is affected; the
   `run_tests.py` default (600s) is unchanged.
5. `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` notes this repo's
   `timeoutPerCommand` override and the rationale for the chosen value.
6. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not raise the global default in `run_tests.py`; use the project-local
  override.
- `.pi/` is project configuration, not agent infrastructure — this change
  adds/modifies only `.pi/test-config.json` and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- **`.pi/test-config.json`** — already exists with `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}`
- **`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`** — needs an addendum noting this
  repo's value and rationale
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — reference only, no change expected

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0** — audit that hit the timeout (AC7 blocked)
- **SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61** — per-project suite extension (`.pi/test-config.json`)
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** — audit auto-execute on cache miss (F3)
- **SA-0MTXLTKFP000ZUZ8** — implement.py finish hardcodes a 600s test timeout (open)
- **SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV** — commit that added `.pi/test-config.json` with 1500s

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` is sufficient. Measured wall-clock is
  ~412s on this machine; under heavy load or CI conditions, suites may take
  longer. 1500s provides ~3.6x margin — adequate but not excessive.
- **Assumption:** No future test additions will cause the suite to exceed 1500s.
  If the suite grows significantly, the timeout should be re-evaluated.
- **Scope creep:** The pre-existing test failure in `test_plan_helpers.py` is
  unrelated to the timeout change. A separate work item should be created to
  fix the stale test parametrisation.
data.title: Raise full-suite per-command timeout so audit auto-execute can complete

data.description:
The audit admission queue accumulates stale tickets from crashed or timed-out audits. A crashed/timed-out audit process never removes its own admission ticket, and the dead-PID cleanup only runs on a 24h TTL prune. With enough stale tickets the queue stays permanently saturated, causing every subsequent audit to fail with 'audit concurrency queue saturated' even when no audit is actually running.

Report rendering has two further defects: the summary mixes parent and child criteria counts, and an unparseable Phase 2 deep-analysis response silently retains the Phase 1 verdicts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. **Stale ticket pruning via dead-PID detection:** `_prune_dead_audit_tickets()` removes audit queue tickets whose owning PID no longer exists (`ProcessLookupError`), returning the count pruned. It is called at admission time and on the slow wait path. Malformed, non-audit, and live-PID entries are left untouched.
2. **Own-ticket cleanup on TimeoutError:** `_acquire_audit_slot()` removes its own admission ticket from the queue before raising `TimeoutError`, so a failed admission never leaves a stale ticket behind.
3. **Parent-only verdict counting:** The report summary counts only the parent item's own acceptance criteria (`ac_results`), never including child criteria. With 2 partial parent ACs and 3 partial child ACs the header reads '2 of 2', not '5 of 2'.
4. **Phase 2 parse-failure disclosure:** When Phase 2 deep-analysis output cannot be parsed, affected ACs are degraded to `partial` with explicit 'could not be parsed' evidence and Phase 2 is marked incomplete. A valid empty JSON array (`[]`) is not a parse failure and preserves the Phase 1 verdict contract.
data.title: Audit runner: stale queue tickets saturate admission and silently keep stale Phase 1 verdicts

## Goal

Fix `_run_eslint_findings_check` and `_run_eslint_fix_mode` in `linter_runner.py` to filter file targets to JS/TS extensions before invoking eslint, preventing false parsing errors on `.py` and other non-JS/TS files.

## Root Cause

- `_run_eslint_findings_check` (line 351): `cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]` passes raw `files` with no extension filter.
- `_run_eslint_fix_mode` (lines 722, 727): same gap in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd`.
- ESLint v6.4.0 tries to parse `.py` files as JavaScript and emits "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scoped eslint runs filter file targets to JS/TS extensions; a `.py`-only changed-file list produces zero eslint findings (eslint skipped or given no JS/TS targets).
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` filters `files` to JS/TS extensions (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`) before building the eslint command.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` returns `[]` (skips eslint) when no JS/TS targets remain after filtering.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` filters both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` to JS/TS extensions only.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` returns `(empty_findings, False)` when no JS/TS targets remain.
- [ ] Non-JS/TS files in the changed-file list are silently skipped (no false-positive findings).
- [ ] Whole-project mode (no explicit files list) is unaffected — it already defaults to JS extensions.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — functions to fix: `_run_eslint_findings_check`, `_run_eslint_fix_mode`
- `skill/code_review/tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — unit tests (see SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ)

## Implementation Notes

- Add a constant `ESLINT_EXTENSIONS = (".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".ts", ".tsx")` near the top of the file (or inline in each function).
- In `_run_eslint_findings_check`, before building the command:

  ```python
  if files:
      js_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(ESLINT_EXTENSIONS)]
      if not js_files:
          return []
      cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in js_files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  else:
      cmd = ["eslint", str(root), "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  ```

- In `_run_eslint_fix_mode`, apply the same filter in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` closures.
- Follow the existing ruff guard pattern at line 392: `py_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(("...",))]`
data.title: Fix: filter eslint to JS/TS extensions in scoped-lint path

## Goal

Add a regression/integration test proving that a scoped lint run whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding, exercising the real command-construction path (not mocked) with a stub runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An audit whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding (regression).
- [ ] The test invokes `run_eslint` (or the public linter entry point) with a `.py`-only `files` list and a stub `runner` that records the constructed command.
- [ ] Assertion: the recorded command contains no `.py` target (eslint is skipped entirely when no JS/TS files remain).
- [ ] No finding has `severity` of `"high"` or `"critical"` for the `.py`-only scope.
- [ ] Test lives in `skill/code_review/tests/` and passes via the standard test runner.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — public entry point(s) to exercise
- `skill/code_review/tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — shared test module

## Dependencies

- Depends on the implementation fix SA-0MUDD7BHE006V3RI and the unit tests SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ.

## Implementation Notes

- Use a stub `runner` callable that returns a controlled result and records the command list, so the test asserts real filtering behaviour without requiring eslint on PATH.
- Assert the `.py` path never appears in any eslint invocation command.
data.title: Regression test: .py-only scoped lint skips eslint

## Problem statement

The refactor skill's auto-fix path invokes the bare `eslint` binary. On this
machine that resolves to a legacy system eslint (v6.x) which reads
`.eslintrc.json` and has no TypeScript parser, so every `.ts`/`.tsx` file
produces an unavoidable "Parsing error" and pollutes code-quality output with
false findings.

## Users

Engineering team members and AI agents running `/skill:refactor` (including the
scheduled refactor run).

**User stories:**
- As an agent running the refactor skill, I want eslint auto-fix to use the
  project's configured eslint (flat config + TypeScript parser) so JS/TS files
  are linted correctly.
- As a producer reviewing refactor output, I want no false "Parsing error"
  findings caused by the wrong eslint binary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_build_eslint_fix_cmd()` returns a command beginning `npx eslint` (not the
   bare `eslint`), preserving the existing `--fix --format json --quiet` flags
   and the supplied file list.
2. `auto_fix_files()` continues to dispatch the eslint fix command for JS/TS
   files through `_build_eslint_fix_cmd()`.
3. Existing refactor auto-fix tests pass (`tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py`).
4. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- No behavioural change for ruff/other linters.
- No new dependency; `npx` is already available in the toolchain.

## Risks & Assumptions

- Assumption: `npx eslint` resolves the project-local eslint from
  `node_modules` (or fetches a compatible version), which loads
  `eslint.config.js` with the TypeScript parser.
- Risk: without network access and without a local eslint, `npx` may fail; the
  existing `probe_linter` gate marks eslint unavailable in that case.
data.title: Refactor skill: run eslint via npx so project flat config and TypeScript parser are used

## Goal

Promote the current `dev` branch to `main` through the gated ship workflow,
publishing all `in_review` work accumulated since the last release.

## Users

**User stories:**
- As a producer, I want `dev` promoted to `main` via the gated, PR-based release
  so all shipped work is published and versioned.
- As an operator, I want each release gating step recorded (merge hash, PR URL)
  on a tracking work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All ship gating checks pass (unmerged branches, audit readiness, critical
   items, worklog refs, producer review, final validation).
2. A `--no-ff` merge commit promotes `dev` to `main` via a PR.
3. The release is verified: tag `v<version>` exists on origin and is an ancestor
   of `origin/main`.
4. `dev` is synced with `main` after the merge.
5. The merge hash and PR URL are recorded on this work item.
6. Eligible `in_review`/`completed` items (`needsProducerReview=false`) are
   closed.

## Constraints

- No direct pushes to `main`; release only via the PR merge.
- No bypass of required status checks.

## Risks & Assumptions

- Assumption: the four producer-review-flagged items are approved before the
  release is re-run.
data.title: Release: promote dev -> main
